content:
Grace O'Connor: Dropping this here for quick feedback from AEs on the outreach cadence templates v1 (Day 0/2/5/10). What’s working / what feels spammy / objections you’re seeing? Also @Markus Klein can we get 2–3 SE-approved snippets for “benchmarking/perf” positioning?

Stephanie Nguyen: +1. Please be brutally honest. We’re trying to keep this PLG-friendly and not freak people out.

Avery Johnson: I ran Day 0 + Day 2 on 3 accounts this week. Tone is mostly fine but the Day 2 subject line (“Following up again”) reads like generic SDR automation. I’d suggest subject like “quick check: scaling Redwood usage?” or “performance question re: your 429s” (if we have that signal).

Ben Carter: Noted on subject lines. We can conditionalize by signal type (scale vs reliability vs security). The current templates are too one-size-fits-all.

Avery Johnson: Timing: Day 0 is good if it’s within a few hours of the signal firing. If we wait overnight it feels disconnected (“why are you emailing me now?”). Day 2 is fine. Day 5 call feels early for some self-serve folks unless we have clear pain (429s / latency regressions / multi-workspace explosion).

Isabelle Laurent: +1 on aligning the touch to “why now.” If we can’t reference a specific trigger without being creepy, we should at least say “saw you’re scaling usage recently” not “noticed you viewed X doc.”

Stephanie Nguyen: Agree. No “we saw you clicked…” language. We should anchor in value: “help you keep latency stable / reduce unit cost / avoid throttling.”

Rachel Kim: Adding from CS POV: for accounts already assigned to a CSM, please do NOT have the cadence auto-fire without notifying CS first. We got a couple “why is Sales emailing me?” pings last month.

Jasmine Liu: +1. If it’s an expansion signal on an existing customer, CS should be looped in before Day 0 goes out. Even a 1-hour heads up in Slack is better than surprise.

Grace O'Connor: Makes sense. For pilot we can add a guardrail: if `CS Owner` exists, task routes to CSM + AE with “coordinate first” copy.

Avery Johnson: Objections I’m hearing:
1) “We’re just testing / not ready to talk to sales.”
2) “We’re cost sensitive; just want cheapest tokens.”
3) “We got 429s but we’ll just add retries / throttle ourselves.”

Avery Johnson: For #1, current email pushes meeting too hard. Suggest CTA: “Want a 10-min sanity check on scaling options?” with a low-commitment vibe.

Ben Carter: Totally. The Day 0 CTA should be “offer help” not “book demo.” We can move meeting link to Day 2/5.

Stephanie Nguyen: Re: 429 objection, we need a clean explanation that Dedicated isn’t “enterprise upsell,” it’s a reliability + throughput control. People assume it’s just paying more.

Grace O'Connor: @Markus Klein can you drop language on: “what we can do in a benchmark + what you’ll learn + how fast.”

Markus Klein: Yep. Here are a few SE-safe snippets you can paste (adjust as needed):

Markus Klein: Snippet A (reliability/429s):
“Happy to run a quick throughput/limits check with you. In ~20 minutes we can look at your request pattern (burst vs steady), then I can share what capacity and batching settings would eliminate rate-limit friction. If it makes sense, we can spin up a short benchmark on Dedicated to validate sustained TPS + p95 latency.”

Markus Klein: Snippet B (performance/latency):
“If latency is a key UX constraint, we can help you set a target (e.g., p95 under X ms at Y concurrency) and run a benchmark against that. We’ll compare Hosted vs Dedicated settings (batching, caching, model variant) so you know the exact cost/latency tradeoff before committing to anything.”

Markus Klein: Snippet C (cost/perf):
“If your main goal is lower $/token without quality loss, we can propose 1–2 serving configs (batching/caching/quant profile) and quantify the savings in a small POC. Usually we can get directional results within 1–2 business days.”

Avery Johnson: This is great. Snippet B is money.
(reactions: :thumbsup: x4)

Stephanie Nguyen: +1. Also can we add one line about “no data needed beyond synthetic prompts” for cautious folks?

Markus Klein: Good call. Add-on sentence:
“We can start with a synthetic prompt set and your target traffic shape—no production data required—then iterate if you want to validate against real prompts later.”

Isabelle Laurent: On cadence spacing: suggest Day 10 “breakup” email should include an explicit opt-out + “we’ll stop reaching out.” Keeps us compliant + less annoying.

Ben Carter: Agree. We’ll add “If now’s not the right time, reply ‘no’ and I’ll close the loop.” (Or similar.)

Avery Johnson: Another note: Day 5 call talk track is too feature-y. Needs 3 questions up top:
- “What’s the user-facing latency target?”
- “Is traffic spiky or steady?”
- “What happens when you hit limits (429/retries/timeouts)?”

Grace O'Connor: Love that. We’ll tighten the call script to discovery-first.

Rachel Kim: For existing customers, include a line like “looping in your CSM @name” so they don’t think they’re being re-sold.

Jasmine Liu: +1 and please avoid scheduling over active support escalations. If there’s an open Sev ticket, CS should own first touch.

Stephanie Nguyen: Action items:
- Grace/Ben: revise templates with signal-specific subject lines + softer Day 0 CTA + explicit opt-out on breakup.
- Isabelle: confirm wording boundaries re: “how we learned” (no doc-click callouts).
- Markus: drop these snippets into the playbook doc.
- CS: share the exact rule for when we treat as “expansion” vs “new conversion.”

Grace O'Connor: I’ll post v1.1 draft in this channel tomorrow and tag a few of you for final eyes.
